To assess the quality of a validator against the given task contracts, we propose an independent-audit approach for the validator by (1) construction of audit oracle: labeling a candidate as PASS or FAIL based on three s
For semantic correctness, reference-calibrated stress tests check output correctness on valid inputs for a candidate.
For implementation integrity, reference and candidate execution traces are used to determine specific library uses.
For measurement integrity, timing checks assess whether the reported runtime reflects the full time needed to complete the candidate's computation.
We apply our approach to assess the quality of six validators and 716 candidates from seven corpora, including constructed controls.
The evaluation results show that our approach helps assess the existing six validators to have nontrivial false-reject rates.
